# Bond ladder: trade fact sheets (for writing your own Trading Notes)

**These are research notes, not Trading Notes.** The competition rules say
"Work generated by an AI program may not be submitted as the team's own", and
any AI use must be recorded in the Works Cited pages (Rules & Roles page,
checked 7 Oct 2026). Use these sheets to understand and verify each trade, then
write each Trading Note yourself, in your own words. Don't copy sentences from
here.

## Rules for the notes themselves

Sources: Competition Guide p.3; Trading Notes Analysis pp.1-2.

1. **WInS asks for the note before the trade executes.** Write it then, using
   the price you see at that moment ("about $21.73"), not the later fill.
2. **Never edit a note after the trade.** Your 23 Oct analysis must quote three
   notes exactly as they appear in WInS, and the organizers verify this.
3. **Cover four things:**
   - the purpose of the trade;
   - how it fits the strategy;
   - the research or analysis behind it;
   - its role (growth, liquidity, risk management or future funding).
4. **Length:** WInS allows up to **300 characters** per note, spaces
   included (seen in WInS by the user, 7 Oct 2026). That is about 45-55
   words. Write 2-3 tight sentences:
   - the purpose (which payment) and the strategy fit;
   - one piece of evidence (the yield, or the alternative rejected);
   - one risk.
   Abbreviations like "Jan 2042" or "5.6% yield" are fine. Count the
   characters before you submit.
5. **Your reflections** for the three notes you pick (100 words or fewer each,
   due 23 Oct) must also be your own. The AI policy says not to use AI for
   personal reflection.

**Official example (Trading Notes Analysis p.2), for style only:** "We are
purchasing shares of an intermediate-term U.S. Treasury bond ETF to reduce
portfolio volatility and begin preparing for Laura's future operating
commitment. The position provides income and greater stability than equities,
although interest-rate changes may affect its value. This trade supports our
plan to balance continued growth with reliable future cash flows as the
residency funding date approaches."

## Facts that apply to every bond trade (verify before using)

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Laura's payments | 10 x $50,000, start of each year 2033-2042, fixed nominal | Case study pp.2-3 |
| Strategy | Option 3 floor rule, m = 2. Bonds protect the payments; stocks = 2 x cushion | Structure model v4 |
| Bond share | 33.6% of the portfolio at a 5.24% blended yield (about $100,800 of $300,000) | Structure model plus WInS quotes, 7 Oct |
| Sizing rule | Each payment gets bond money in proportion to its present value, so each holding grows to about $17,245 | Calculation, 7 Oct |
| Treasury yields, 24 Sep 2026 | 5-yr 5.03%, 7-yr 5.10%, 10-yr 5.18% | Federal Reserve H.15 (M02 SRC-01) |
| Projections | CBO 10-yr about 4.4% from 2031 (secondary summary); FOMC median fed funds 4.1% end-2027 | M02 SRC-06, SRC-02 |
| Why Treasuries | US government credit; paid in USD, so no currency risk; fixed repayment at maturity | |
| Main risk accepted | If yields rise further, we lock in less. Held to maturity, price swings don't affect payments | |

Estimated fund yields come from price changes since July. Check iShares'
"Average Yield to Maturity" before quoting a number, or say "approximately".

## Checklist for each note you write

- [ ] Which of Laura's payments does this fund, and why does this maturity fit it?
- [ ] How does it fit the strategy? (Option 3 floor: bonds secure the payments,
  stocks provide growth.)
- [ ] What research supports it? (the yield you're locking in, and why now)
- [ ] What role does it play? (future funding and risk management)
- [ ] One honest risk or trade-off.
- [ ] 300 characters or fewer (count them), your own wording, written before you click Buy.
